article_content: In a dazzling event set to captivate Shanghai, Burberry is preparing to unveil its largest store in Asia. Although the guest list remains a secret, speculation is rife that celebrities like Cara Delevingne and Suki Waterhouse will be in attendance. These stars have been actively sharing their Shanghai adventures on Instagram, fueling the excitement. The event, dubbed 'London In Shanghai', will take place at a shipping yard in the bustling city. VIPs will be dressed in Burberry's exclusive Gold collection, available only at the new store. The event promises a classic Burberry performance for guests, including private invitees and competition winners. Burberry, known for its leadership in social media, has partnered with WeChat, China's largest social media platform with over 600 million users. Top influencers on WeChat, such as Angelababy and Vicki Zhao, have millions of followers, surpassing even Justin Bieber's Twitter following. The store, located in the Kerry Centre mall in Shanghai's Jing An district, is modeled after the UK Regent Street flagship. It features a vast, open 'landing page' area designed to mimic the Burberry.com website, complete with a free-standing screen displaying catwalk footage and a grand stone staircase. This store is not only the largest in Asia but also boasts the biggest beauty room, watch room, and Prorsum collection. Additionally, it includes interactive mirrors that provide related content when approached with a garment, and an intelligent glass facade that adjusts to weather conditions. The store's furniture and fittings are British-designed, and the window display showcases the Heritage collection, featuring classic trench coats for men and women. The event promises to be a spectacle, blending luxury with cutting-edge technology.

article_content: She was renowned as a Hollywood star and style icon. Now, Audrey Hepburn is to be celebrated with a photography exhibition at London's National Portrait Gallery. An exhibition about the actress's life and career will open in July and include family images of her at ballet practice and pictures taken during her early days working as a model in London. Scroll down for video. Celebration: An exhibition of photos of Audrey Hepburn - including this shot taken by Norman Parkinson in 1955 - will open at the National Portrait Gallery in July 2015. Photographs from Life Magazine, taken during the making of her 1953 film 'Sabrina', will also go on show alongside posters for some of her most famous films. The Belgian-born actress performed at Ciro’s nightclub, which now forms the gallery’s archive and study room, in a series of revues in 1949 and 1950. The gallery’s deputy director Pim Baxter said: 'Audrey Hepburn was one of the world’s most celebrated actresses. I am delighted that the National Portrait Gallery will hold a major photography exhibition exploring the life and work of such a significant and much-loved figure who spent the formative early years of her career in Britain. The exhibition about Audrey's life will include pictures taken during her days working as a model in London - as well as this image, which was a publicity shot for 1954's 'Sabrina'. The exhibition includes this photo taken by Sir Cecil Beaton in 1954. It is particularly appropriate that the exhibition will be staged in such close proximity to where she performed as a young woman at the very start of her career.' The exhibition runs to October 18. As the world continues to celebrate Audrey Hepburn's impeccable style, her granddaughter is continuing her legacy. After spending most of her life out of the spotlight, Emma Ferrer is starting to make herself known. The 20-year-old art student was seen at New York Fashion Week in July strolling past the Lincoln Center accompanied by Harper's Bazaar British editor, Glenda Bailey, who last month crowned Emma as the magazine's September issue cover star. Behind the scenes: Candid shots of Audrey through the ages - including this photo captured in Rome in 1960 by Sir Cecil Beaton - will go on display at the gallery. Emma, whose 54-year-old father is Sean Hepburn Ferrer, Audrey's oldest son, was raised in Los Angeles and is currently in her third year at the Florence Academy of Art, in Italy. And although art is her primary focus, Emma is clearly taking tentative footsteps into the world of fashion as well. Last month's coveted Harper's Bazaar cover saw her effortlessly re-create her grandmother's iconic poses, in a stunning spread shot by Michael Avedon, grandson of legendary photographer Richard Avedon, for whom Audrey was a longtime muse. While her grandmother lost her life to cancer in 1993, a year before Emma was born, there's no denying that her legacy lives on within her. Charting her career: Photographs from magazines, as well as posters for some of her most famous films, will be on display at the London gallery. Right, Hepburn as Breakfast At Tiffany's Holly Golightly character in 1962, by Howell Conant. Left, a portrait taken by Angus McBean in 1950. 'I've been questioning a lot lately what she means to me,' Emma told Harper's Bazaar. 'I knew her image, of course, and that I happened to be, by pure chance, related to her. But as a child I couldn't really relate to Audrey Hepburn, the actress. To me, she was family.' And despite never getting the chance to meet her grandmother, Emma's father Sean told the publication that his daughter's similarities to Audrey are plenty. 'My mother was the same as she was on the screen: unassuming, humble, funny, emotional, strong, delicate,' says the father-of-three, who has also pursued an acting career as well as helping run the Audrey Hepburn Children's Fund. 'Fortunately Emma has much better boundaries than either Mom or I ever had. But the genes are strong - and the comedic gene is alive and well.' For Emma, the associations between her and Hepburn are unavoidable, and it's something she is slowly coming to terms with. 'Sometimes when I was younger, I felt confused toward what having a grandmother like her could mean in my life. But I am now understanding,' she said.

article_content: This haunting photo shows a 21-year-old man posing on a Virginia trestle - just one week before he was struck and killed by a train while walking along the same tracks with his girlfriend. In the image, posted on Instagram, Jonathan Gregoire is seen standing at the edge of the trestle near Lynchburg, where he died, and Victoria Bridges, also 21, was seriously injured on Saturday. Alongside the picture, the Liberty University student wrote lyrics from singer Noah Gunderson's 'Ledges', including: 'Here, I stand in the land of the rocks and the valley, trying to be a better man.' Mr. Gregoire, from Wilbraham, Massachusetts, and Ms. Bridges, from Newport News, were walking along the tracks with a group of friends at around 4:20 PM when a northbound train approached. Although Mr. Gregoire was fatally hit by the vehicle, Ms. Bridges incredibly survived after leaping 100 feet off the railway bridge and landing on the terrain below. Following the impact, the train driver told a dispatcher: 'There were three people that we could see, one beside the tracks, two out on the tracks,' according to ABC News. 'As soon as I got there, it was too late. Then I heard a thump. One of them, looked like a girl, jumped. And I heard the one thump, I’m pretty sure the girl jumped and I might have hit the guy.' Paramedics rushed to the scene, where they found Ms. Bridges lying on the ground. She was airlifted to Lynchburg General Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, WDBJ reported. She remains in a stable condition. Mr. Gregoire was pronounced dead at the scene. On Sunday, it emerged that Mr. Gregoire, a senior majoring in business administration-marketing, had widely spoken of his passion for hiking, exploring, and other outdoor pursuits on social media. He had also recently posted a series of messages about the meaning of life and death, with his last Facebook post reading: 'If life ends in the grave, then we have no ultimate purpose for living.' Another recent message said: 'I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God.' Killed: Mr. Gregoire (pictured, left and right), from Wilbraham, Massachusetts, was walking along the trestle with a group of friends and his girlfriend, Victoria Bridges, on Saturday when a northbound train came. Airlifted: Although Mr. Gregoire was fatally hit by the vehicle, Ms. Bridges (pictured being stretchered away by medics) incredibly survived after leaping 100 feet off the railway bridge and landing on terrain below. Not uncommon: Witnesses say accidents like this are not uncommon for the trestle located above James River at Riverside Park near Lynchburg, VA. According to News Advance, more than one other person was walking along the trestle with Mr. Gregoire and Ms. Bridges when the train approached. However, the others were walking beside the tracks, not on them. Members of the friendship group were seen crying and walking behind the stretcher carrying Ms. Bridges after the incident. Public safety officials were at the scene for approximately two hours. The incident is being investigated by Lynchburg Police Department’s Criminal Investigations Division. Foul play is not suspected, according to ABC News. Robin Chapman, spokesman for Norfolk Southern, told News Advance that many use the trestle as a shortcut home or simply for the view from the trestle. Scene: Public safety officials were at the scene for approximately two hours after the accident. Group: Officials say a group of individuals, all appearing to be in their late teens, were walking along or near the trestle when the northbound train approached. Eerie: Mr. Gregoire had recently posted a series of messages about the meaning of life and death, with his last Facebook post reading: 'If life ends in the grave, then we have no ultimate purpose for living.' An autumnal walk: His post was accompanied by this photo of him and his friends walking in Riverside Park. Witnesses told ABC 13 that incidents like this are becoming common on this particular train trestle located above the James River at Riverside Park. 'It's kind of becoming a problem with, you know, the children and the teenagers that want to come up here and get on the railroad track,' local resident Julie Burgess told ABC 13. 'They're pretty much playing Russian roulette with their life.' In October 2012, a man was struck and killed by a train while crossing the trestle. A year earlier, another Liberty University student died - and their friend was seriously injured - there. Passionate: On Sunday, it emerged that Mr. Gregoire (pictured with two friends), who is majoring in business administration-marketing, had widely spoken of his passion for hiking and exploring on social media. Russian roulette: A local resident said that teens and children walking on the trestle are 'playing Russian roulette with their life.'

article_content: A federal appeals court on Thursday blocked a ruling that deemed the New York Police Department's stop-and-frisk policy unconstitutional. The court also removed Judge Shira A. Scheindlin from the case due to concerns about the appearance of impropriety. The three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit stated that the lower court judge 'ran afoul' of the requirements that judges avoid even the appearance of impropriety. The appeals court cited Scheindlin's media interviews and public statements, which they believed compromised the appearance of partiality. In a related 2007 proceeding, Scheindlin suggested that individuals with proof of inappropriate racial profiling should bring a lawsuit, marking it as related. She added, 'I am sure I am going to get in trouble for saying it, but for $65 you can bring that lawsuit,' according to the ruling. The appeals court also pointed to interviews with the New York Law Journal, The Associated Press, and The New Yorker, where Scheindlin discussed her personal beliefs on the issue and defended her decision. The stop-and-frisk policy, which allows police to stop, question, and frisk individuals deemed suspicious even if they have committed no crime, has sparked significant controversy. Critics argue that the practice is racist and illegal, while law enforcement and other proponents claim it helps reduce crime. In August, Scheindlin ruled that the policy was unconstitutional, stating that it unlawfully targeted blacks and Latinos. She found that police made at least 200,000 stops from 2004 to June 2012 without reasonable suspicion, violating the plaintiffs' Fourth Amendment rights against unreasonable searches and their Fourteenth Amendment rights to equal protection. The appeals court did not rule on the merits of Scheindlin's decision. Michael A. Cardozo, counsel for the New York City Law Office, praised the appeals court's ruling, stating, 'We could not be more pleased with the court's findings,' as it delays a decision on the policy's constitutionality until another judge can review it. The Center for Constitutional Rights, representing the plaintiffs, criticized the ruling, expressing disappointment in the delay of reforms and the removal of Scheindlin from the case. Thursday's ruling effectively stalls the changes mandated by Scheindlin, who ordered that stops be based on reasonable suspicion and conducted in a racially neutral manner. Her ruling also called for the appointment of a former Manhattan prosecutor to develop reforms and a pilot project requiring NYPD patrol officers in five precincts to wear video cameras. Outgoing Mayor Michael Bloomberg supports the stop-and-frisk policy, asserting that it saves lives and reduces crime. NYPD Commissioner Ray Kelly, who had a speech canceled at Brown University due to protests, expressed concern about Scheindlin's partiality and looked forward to further examination of the case. The controversy surrounding the stop-and-frisk policy has extended into the mayoral race. Democratic nominee Bill de Blasio, heavily favored to win, has made his opposition to the policy a central campaign issue. 'I'm extremely disappointed in today's decision. We shouldn't have to wait for reforms that both keep our communities safe and obey the Constitution,' he stated. Republican nominee Joe Lhota praised the ruling, stating, 'Bravo! As I have said all along, Judge Scheindlin's biased conduct corrupted the case, and her decision was not based on the facts.'
translated_content: Um tribunal federal de apelações bloqueou na quinta-feira uma decisão que considerou inconstitucional a política de parar e revistar do Departamento de Polícia de Nova York. O tribunal também removeu a juíza Shira A. Scheindlin do caso devido a preocupações com a aparência de impropriedade. O painel de três juízes do Tribunal de Apelações dos Estados Unidos para o Segundo Circuito declarou que o juiz do tribunal inferior 'contrariou' os requisitos de que os juízes evitem até mesmo a aparência de impropriedade. O tribunal de apelações citou entrevistas à mídia e declarações públicas de Scheindlin, que acreditavam comprometer a aparência de imparcialidade. Em um processo relacionado em 2007, Scheindlin sugeriu que indivíduos com provas de discriminação racial inadequada deveriam entrar com uma ação, marcando-a como relacionada. Ela acrescentou: 'Tenho certeza de que vou me meter em encrenca por dizer isso, mas por $65 você pode entrar com essa ação', de acordo com a decisão. O tribunal de apelações também apontou entrevistas com o New York Law Journal, The Associated Press e The New Yorker, onde Scheindlin discutiu suas crenças pessoais sobre o assunto e defendeu sua decisão. A política de parar e revistar, que permite que a polícia pare, questione e reviste indivíduos considerados suspeitos, mesmo que não tenham cometido nenhum crime, gerou grande controvérsia. Críticos argumentam que a prática é racista e ilegal, enquanto a aplicação da lei e outros defensores afirmam que ajuda a reduzir o crime. Em agosto, Scheindlin decidiu que a política era inconstitucional, afirmando que visava indevidamente negros e latinos. Ela constatou que a polícia fez pelo menos 200.000 paradas de 2004 a junho de 2012 sem suspeita razoável, violando os direitos dos autores da Quarta Emenda contra buscas irrazoáveis e seus direitos da Décima Quarta Emenda à igualdade de proteção. O tribunal de apelações não decidiu sobre os méritos da decisão de Scheindlin. Michael A. Cardozo, conselheiro do Gabinete de Advocacia da Cidade de Nova York, elogiou a decisão do tribunal de apelações, afirmando: 'Não poderíamos estar mais satisfeitos com as conclusões do tribunal', pois adia uma decisão sobre a constitucionalidade da política até que outro juiz possa revisá-la. O Centro de Direitos Constitucionais, representando os autores, criticou a decisão, expressando decepção com o atraso nas reformas e a remoção de Scheindlin do caso. A decisão de quinta-feira efetivamente adia as mudanças determinadas por Scheindlin, que ordenou que as paradas fossem baseadas em suspeita razoável e conduzidas de maneira racialmente neutra. Sua decisão também pediu a nomeação de um ex-promotor de Manhattan para desenvolver reformas e um projeto piloto exigindo que policiais do NYPD em cinco distritos usem câmeras de vídeo. O prefeito Michael Bloomberg apoia a política de parar e revistar, afirmando que salva vidas e reduz o crime. O comissário do NYPD, Ray Kelly, que teve um discurso cancelado na Brown University devido a protestos, expressou preocupação com a parcialidade de Scheindlin e aguarda um exame mais aprofundado do caso. A controvérsia em torno da política de parar e revistar estendeu-se à corrida pela prefeitura. O candidato democrata Bill de Blasio, fortemente favorito para vencer, transformou sua oposição à política em uma questão central da campanha. 'Estou extremamente decepcionado com a decisão de hoje. Não deveríamos ter que esperar por reformas que mantenham nossas comunidades seguras e obedeçam à Constituição', declarou. O candidato republicano Joe Lhota elogiou a decisão, afirmando: 'Bravo! Como sempre disse, a conduta tendenciosa da juíza Scheindlin corrompeu o caso e sua decisão não se baseou nos fatos.'

article_content: Do you know your child's favorite nursery rhyme, family game, or TV character? What truly makes them laugh? Recent research indicates that one in six fathers find it challenging to engage in play with their children. In response, a prominent national nursery is providing lessons to help parents enjoy quality playtime with their kids. Busy Bees day nursery group, with numerous playgroups across the UK, offers these coaching sessions to enhance parents' playtime skills when children return home. How to Play: Aleeza Haider, three, and Binuthi Kannangara, three, along with Chef Robert England, are pictured learning essential skills at Busy Bees nursery in Rotherham, South Yorkshire. The study, conducted by toy company Playmobil, reveals that many parents of young children are concerned about not spending enough time playing with them. Over six out of ten parents admit they play with their children only occasionally, with a third of fathers citing lack of time as the main issue. The course aims to teach parents of babies and toddlers how to play more effectively. A spokesperson noted, 'When parents are new, some find playtime easier than others. We encourage them to stay and play to see what their children enjoy. Some need ideas for games and activities, while others want to learn how to interact best with their child.' 'Parents often worry about being good cooks for their children and whether their child is developing properly, but playtime is a moment for both parents and children to enjoy. We have been operating for 30 years, so there is a wealth of experience for parents to benefit from.' The research also found that over nine out of ten parents buy electronic toys for their children, but a third of mothers admit to being confused by these high-tech gadgets and games. Peter Morley, a father of two children attending Busy Bees nursery in Guiseley, West Yorks, commented, 'I hope my children think I'm doing okay. Busy Bees nurseries offer stay and play sessions, which would be a great starting point for parents needing encouragement and ideas.' Sharon Pearce, an independent play therapist, added, 'Parents should play with their children to improve the parent-child relationship and enhance behavior and mental health. Parents face a lot of pressure, but playtime is more important than household chores. Playing doesn't need to be expensive; it's about imagination, like using a cardboard box and bits of paper. It's like a bank—the more time you invest in playing with your children, the better the outcomes will be.' Margaret Randles, Co-Founder and Managing Director of Busy Bees, stated, 'When a parent chooses Busy Bees as their childcare partner, we believe we have an obligation to provide support and advice. As a parent myself, I know every day brings different challenges, and sometimes you feel like you're winging it. Having someone to confide in or provide reassurance is helpful. I consider myself fortunate to have had nursery expertise readily available when I had my first child. We want our parents to know we are here to support them. That's what a true partnership is.'

article_content: (CNN) -- Australia battled back to secure a 1-1 draw with South Korea on Friday, pushing both teams closer to the Asian Cup quarterfinals in Qatar. The result leaves both nations with four points from two matches in Group C, ahead of the day's other game where 10-man Bahrain defeated India 5-2, thanks to four goals from Ismaeel Abdulatif. South Korea, winners of the first two Asian Cup tournaments in 1956 and 1960, took the lead in the 24th minute at Doha's Al Gharafa Stadium through Koo Ja-cheol. The 21-year-old midfielder scored his third goal of the tournament, following his double in Korea's opening 2-1 win over Bahrain. Ji Dong-won collected a long ball and passed it to Koo, who finished smoothly. Both teams had several scoring opportunities before Mile Jedinak equalized in the 62nd minute. The midfielder, who plays for Turkish club Genclerbirligi, headed home after Korea failed to clear a corner from Luke Wilkshire, with Lucas Neill nodding the ball back across the goal. 'We could have won the game. If you look at the general performance of our team, then we should have won,' South Korea coach Cho Kwang-Rae told the Asian Cup website. 'We controlled the game mostly so in that aspect we have improved a lot. I am pleased about that and if we can continue to develop that part of our game then it will be much better for us as we move forward.' 'My team, I'm very happy with their performance. Our game plan was to close them down in midfield and that was mostly achieved,' said Australia's German coach Holger Osieck. 'What I found encouraging was we created a lot of chances.' Abdulatif's four goals boosted Bahrain's hopes of reaching the quarterfinals. The 24-year-old forward scored three times in 19 first-half minutes against India. Faouzi Aaish opened the scoring with an eighth-minute penalty, but India equalized through Gouramangi Singh within a minute. Abdulatif then capitalized on a mistake by India goalkeeper Subrata Paul, was set up by Jaycee John for his second, and completed his hat-trick before halftime. India thought they had reduced the deficit after halftime, but Renedy Singh's effort was ruled not to have crossed the line. Sunil Chhetri immediately made it 4-2 after Abhishek Yadav hit the woodwork. Aaish was sent off for diving, but Abdulatif secured the win with a solo effort 13 minutes from time. The final round on Tuesday sees South Korea face India and Australia take on Bahrain.
translated_content: (CNN) -- A Austrália lutou para garantir um empate de 1-1 com a Coreia do Sul na sexta-feira, empurrando ambas as equipes para mais perto das quartas de final da Copa da Ásia no Qatar. O resultado deixa ambas as nações com quatro pontos em dois jogos no Grupo C, à frente do outro jogo do dia, onde o Bahrain, com 10 homens, derrotou a Índia por 5-2, graças a quatro gols de Ismaeel Abdulatif. A Coreia do Sul, vencedora dos dois primeiros torneios da Copa da Ásia em 1956 e 1960, assumiu a liderança no 24º minuto no Estádio Al Gharafa, em Doha, através de Koo Ja-cheol. O meio-campista de 21 anos marcou seu terceiro gol no torneio, após sua dupla na vitória de abertura da Coreia por 2-1 sobre o Bahrain. Ji Dong-won recolheu uma bola longa e passou para Koo, que finalizou suavemente. Ambas as equipes tiveram várias oportunidades de marcar antes de Mile Jedinak empatar no 62º minuto. O meio-campista, que joga pelo clube turco Genclerbirligi, cabeceou para dentro depois que a Coreia não conseguiu afastar um canto de Luke Wilkshire, com Lucas Neill acenando a bola de volta pelo gol. 'Poderíamos ter ganhado o jogo. Se você olhar para o desempenho geral da nossa equipe, então deveríamos ter ganhado', disse o técnico da Coreia do Sul, Cho Kwang-Rae, ao site da Copa da Ásia. 'Controlamos o jogo na maior parte do tempo, então nesse aspecto melhoramos muito. Estou satisfeito com isso e, se pudermos continuar a desenvolver essa parte do nosso jogo, será muito melhor para nós à medida que avançamos.' 'Estou muito feliz com o desempenho da minha equipe. Nosso plano de jogo era fechá-los no meio-campo e isso foi amplamente alcançado', disse o técnico alemão da Austrália, Holger Osieck. 'O que achei encorajador foi que criamos muitas chances.' Os quatro gols de Abdulatif aumentaram as esperanças do Bahrain de chegar às quartas de final. O atacante de 24 anos marcou três vezes em 19 minutos na primeira metade contra a Índia. Faouzi Aaish abriu o placar com um pênalti aos oito minutos, mas a Índia empatou com Gouramangi Singh em menos de um minuto. Abdulatif então capitalizou um erro do goleiro indiano Subrata Paul, foi montado por Jaycee John para o segundo e completou o hat-trick antes do intervalo. A Índia pensou ter reduzido a diferença no segundo tempo, mas o esforço de Renedy Singh foi considerado não ter cruzado a linha. Sunil Chhetri imediatamente fez 4-2 após Abhishek Yadav acertar a trave. Aaish foi expulso por mergulhar, mas Abdulatif garantiu a vitória com um esforço solo a 13 minutos do final. A rodada final na terça-feira vê a Coreia do Sul enfrentar a Índia e a Austrália enfrentar o Bahrain.
